title: Witness compatibility condition
statement:
Fix a cartesian square $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ of schemes, with $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$ and $g':X'\to X$, [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] and an adic coefficient datum $(A,I)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], with $P_n=A/I^n$ for $n\geq1$. Use the four ambient finite-level functors $Rf_{*,n}$, $Rf'_{*,n}$, $Lg_n^*$ and $Lg_n'^*$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], with source-target pairs $(X,Y)$, $(X',Y')$, $(Y,Y')$ and $(X,X')$, respectively. Test them on the bounded constructible input categories of [def-weil-pbc-finite-level-amplification], defined in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. No restriction of a functor to a bounded constructible output category is assumed unless separately supplied by AMP.

For a scheme $T$, write $r^T_n(M)=M\otimes^L_{(P_{n+1})_T}(P_n)_T$ for coefficient reduction, using the quotient-coefficient sheaves and normalization maps of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. A normalized tower has isomorphisms $\theta_n:r^T_nK_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_n$, with the quotient cocycle for successive reductions. A compatible etale-origin witness consists of the retained pairs $(L_n,\alpha_n)$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness] and isomorphisms $\beta_n:L_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}L_n$, with the quotient cocycle, such that
$$\alpha_n\circ\nu_T^*(\beta_n)=\theta_n\circ r^T_n(\alpha_{n+1}).$$
Here $L_n\in D^+(T_{\Et},P_n)$, and the tensors on the etale side use its constant coefficient sheaves. Derived change of coefficient sheaves is [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The source of the displayed equality is identified by the tensor comparison for the ringed comparison morphism $\nu_T$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], using the inverse-image coefficient identification of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Thus both sides are maps from $\nu_T^*(L_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n)$ to $K_n$.

Define $\mathrm{WIT}(\square)$, relative to the fixed coefficient datum, to mean the following condition for each of the four functor families $F_n:D(T_{\Proet},P_n)\to D(S_{\Proet},P_n)$ above, on the full input subcategory of $D^b_c(T_{\Proet},P_{n+1})$ consisting of objects whose reduction also belongs to $D^b_c(T_{\Proet},P_n)$. The output is taken in the ambient derived category; the output witnesses required below are bounded below. Coefficient reduction commutes with $F_n$ through natural isomorphisms
$$\rho_n:r^S_nF_{n+1}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_nr^T_n,$$
compatible with identity reductions and composition of quotient maps. Thus the output normalization is required to be
$$\theta'_n=F_n(\theta_n)\circ\rho_n(K_{n+1}).$$
For every normalized input tower with bounded constructible levels equipped with compatible etale-origin witnesses, the functor carries the retained witness data to output pairs $(L'_n,\alpha'_n)$ for $F_nK_n$, equipped with isomorphisms $\beta'_n:L'_{n+1}\otimes^L_{P_{n+1}}P_n\xrightarrow{\sim}L'_n$ satisfying the quotient cocycle and
$$\alpha'_n\circ\nu_S^*(\beta'_n)=\theta'_n\circ r^S_n(\alpha'_{n+1}).$$
Carrying witness data means a functor on witnessed towers over the levelwise functor $F_\bullet$: a morphism of witnessed towers is a pair of compatible levelwise maps $u_n:K_n\to\widetilde K_n$ and $v_n:L_n\to\widetilde L_n$ with $u_n\alpha_n=\widetilde\alpha_n\nu_T^*(v_n)$, and the underlying output maps are $F_n(u_n)$. This is a compatibility predicate, not an assertion that these comparisons or transported witnesses exist for every square.

note:
*Source note:* no Stacks Project entry states this predicate: the
etale-origin witnesses are the blueprint's device for Stacks' hypothesis in
Theorem 61.30.1 ([Tag 09C9](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C9)) that
$K\otimes^L_\Lambda\underline{\Lambda/I^n}$ be bounded below with cohomology
sheaves coming from the etale site. The per-level existence of such an
origin is Stacks' Lemma 61.29.2 ([Tag
09C2](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/09C2)) (4): for a constructible
$K$ on a quasi-compact $X$ there are $a,b$ with $K=\Rlim K_n$, each $K_n$ of
tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ with constructible cohomology sheaves, and
$K_n=\epsilon^{-1}L_n$ for some $L_n\in D_{ctf}(X_{\Et},\Lambda/I^n)$.
Difference: Stacks states this for a single object, and neither asserts that
the $L_n$ are compatible over $n$ nor tracks maps $\alpha_n$ as in
[def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness]; the blueprint adds the compatibility
predicate $\mathrm{WIT}(\square)$.

proof.text: For the supporting theorem pbcRestriction_isRightAdjoint, form ordinary scalar extension by composing sectionwise ModuleCat.extendScalars with sheafification. Its adjunction to restriction is Sheaf.adjunction. Commuting restriction past sheafification, use ModuleCat.extendScalarsCompRestrictScalarsIso and the sheafification tensor comparison to identify extension followed by restriction with tensoring by the constant coefficient module sheaf. CochainComplex.acyclic_tensorRight_of_kFlat sends acyclic K-flat complexes to acyclic complexes under this tensor functor. Faithful exact restriction reflects acyclicity. Functor.PreservesKFlatQuasiIso.mk' and Adjunction.derivedAdjunction then give the derived adjunction; exactness identifies the right derived restriction with mapDerivedCategory. These are existing proved source-library declarations, used directly in the fixed-ring presentation.

For identity and composition of witnessed tower maps, apply functoriality and associativity to the theta, beta and origin squares. Extensionality on the two levelwise components proves the category laws; proof fields agree by proof irrelevance.

For pbcWitnessedInput_memReductionDomain, the next level is bounded constructible by the input property. At the current level choose the existing constructible realization witness and compose its realization isomorphism with the realization of theta inverse. This gives the required essential-image witness for the reduction.

For pbcComparisonReductionMap_isIso, first prove ordinary scalar-extension compatibility by iterated mates: comparison direct image commutes strictly with restriction and coextension, and the sectionwise restriction/coextension triangle identifies the second mate with the identity. Conjugation then makes the ordinary extension mate invertible. Extend the existing comparison-flatness argument to arbitrary coefficient rings: use the full relation kernel and express each local tensor lift as a finite sum; finite generation of the full kernel is unnecessary. Comparison inverse image thus preserves flat terms of functorial K-flat resolutions. Compute scalar left derived functors on these resolutions. The unit identities for the derived scalar adjunction and the localization comparison identities show that the derived mate is the image of the ordinary mate, up to the invertible resolution comparison maps. Every derived object is isomorphic to such a resolution, so naturality proves invertibility everywhere. Finally, uniqueness of left adjoints transports this conclusion to the fixed chosen scalar-extension adjunctions used by pbcComparisonReductionMap. All intermediate helpers are proved privately in the same module; no new holed statements are introduced.
